data: Great game and story was amazing as well, Highly recommend
Good game, fun gameplay, great story
All in all, well worth the price and I highly recommend it
Love the graphics and the soundtrack is awesome:)
My only complaint is the lack of replayability
The cool creepiness of the beginning is replaced by a boring tidium of poor fetch quests and absolutely no real incentive to do anything
this is not worth the price
unfortunately, it is just not for me - the gameplay is too repetitive for my taste
It's incredibly dull and boring gameplay that you need to do to progress
The story (mystery) is very short and I found it underwhelming
And there's not really a plot or interesting characters to speak of
And there're lot of other black woman characters that seem to have been inserted just to make a statement
There isn't even really any interesting choice in how you spend your time: fishing makes you money
certain fish make you more money, here's a small set of reflex based games to reel them in faster
Just don't buy it at full price
I ultimately stopped because the upgrade was so repetitive and I couldn't figure out what the point was
No challenge or smartness to it, just a fairly gentle RNG grind
Explore the game without external help makes the game drag so long, and the repetitive gameplay doesn't make the process any more pleasant
I have no problem with the gameplay,
The fishing gameplay basically exists just to make you feel you are doing barely something
I need something more gripping, whether it's story or gameplay, and this one lacks both

Welcome to the wild and varied world of fishing!
Tired of your flimsy rickety rod?
Tired of your slow and safe engines?
Try,

BARGAINING WITH THE GREAT OLD ONES

100% all achievements, i love this game this is a game i love

A great game, really nicely unique and well made with an interesting story.
However, considering I have completed it and then some within a space of 10 hours, I would definitely only recommend buying it at a vastly reduced price.
A beautiful game about life at sea. A casual yet daunting experience. Wonder, adventure and dread are the three main feelings I get while playing this game. 9/10 for me.

It wasn't a long time, but it was a good one. If you enjoy the play cycle of relaxation mixed with sporadic panic attacks, this is your game. For the completionist, there's quite the variety of species and mutations to discover. If you Obsessively fill your pokedex, you'll enjoy a longer playtime, but as for myself, I wasn't compelled to complete my collection after finishing the game. I highly recommend avoiding guides, as they will vastly shorten your playtime (although I found myself stuck in a couple locations and had to research the solution).
I havent even finished the game yet, but I can surely say, that this game is good, unique and able to create call of the Cthulhu like atmosphere. Quality indie adventure game, should try this out.

Fun little game about catching fishes and running away from the horrors of the sea. Gameplay loop super simple, get fish / resources, upgrade your ship for better equipment -> ship goes faster and you can get better and more exotic fish. Some may find it repetitive but I thought it was kinda chill. Also some lovecraftian / eldritch horrors to challenge your fishing, those were cool. And low-poly artstyle suits the game well.

Overall good fun chill fishing game. And not too long either, roughly 8~12hrs to complete.

Black Salt Games made something pretty spectacular here. This is a "Lovecraftian Deadliest Catch" that blends exploration and mystery into a really unique experience. At first you spend your days fishing in a harbor and selling basic catches just to slowly upgrade the boat and this is the part where I was questioning the game play. Once you are brave enough to explore...that's when this game becomes addictive!

Each upgrade let's you explore a new cluster of islands with their own unique vibe/environment w/ a different set dangers, new species of crabs and fish and also with fresh mechanics that are introduced naturally as the story progresses. The Fish Almanac and the want to discover all the aberrations was the truly addictive part + the story had enough mystery behind it that keeps REELING you in.

The art style behind this game was beautiful and it reminded me of a Supergiant game. Well done Black Salt. This game comes highly recommended if you are trying to scratch the fishing itch + want to enjoy the scenery and explore the world with a touch of horror sprinkled on top.

Fantastic games, finished it in one setting basically. The UI, boat handling, upgrades, exploration and mood is superb, the story is nice and keeps your attention.

Took me around 12 hours to finish it and i did most of what's available. didn't catch every fish but i thoroughly enjoyed the experience. A bit on the pricey side given how short it is. but these days i'd take short and sweet over grindy and long anytime.

This is great! Definitely loving the intregue built into the game and also appreciate that I can take it at my own pace - go exploring, work on upgrades, fish for new things whilst having podcasts and such in the background
I am usually really thalassophobic, so I was expecting to go into this game and get my butt scared off. That did happen but it was a fantastic story 10/10 and I loved the mechanics.

Lots of good to say. Fantastic art direction, riveting gameplay loop, intriguing storyline and characters, and the concept is very much my type. Everything is put together in a way that is of extraordinary quality. Most days bring something new and even the ones that don't are well spent. It seems weird to say that since so much of the sea is empty and early-game boat movement is slow but the faults are less noticeable while in the moment. When I think about what actually happens from day-to-day, progression seems harshly minimal and the most interesting moments are short-lived. Navigating at nighttime is too intimidating. It sucks to see a cool mysterious who-knows-what off in the distance and yet death comes so quickly or it's too scary to keep going and I end up sailing back to a port. The grind to find the mysterious parts to make my little boat more capable also seems to involve a lot of elusive sailing to nowhere. Also, there is apparently no Cthulhu (or at least no clear and obvious Cthulhu front and center) which is madness for a game that has Lovecraftian stated in the description.

I think it's probably worth the grind of upgrades and I'd change my opinion with more time and after getting over the initial early game struggles, not unlike Death Stranding. Both games are weirdly similar, dark yet cozy.
Really a great game. Try it 100% while its on sale. DLCs are also good and make it replayable. Currently trying to 100% it as i played through the story twice on console.

Beautiful game, amazing gameplay. I absolutely love the art style, simple incredible. The gameplay is simple yet engaging. The horror elements really keep you on your toes. My favorite is the randomly spawned neutral animals, really got me excited whenever they showed up.

I absolutely love this game.

game of the year.

or, at least, it should be.

if you want a beautiful game with a stellar soundtrack, unique gameplay, suspense 'till the very end, and an absolutely riveting story... look no further.
This game is so fun and addictive, I just couldn't stop playing! Game has charming atmosphere and excellent mechanics.

Dredge is the best fishing minigame to ever have a lovecraftian horror subplot attached to it. The horrors beyond human comprehension can wait, I have crab traps to check and cod to catch.

Jokes aside, the game really is phenomenal. It has very well-crafted gameplay systems; depending on how much time you sink into making money, upgrades and cautious exploration, you can confront the horror gameplay at your own pace and manage the level of stress and frantic moments to whatever you're comfortable with. The wide variety of different fishing minigames depending on the fish type makes the gameplay loop of fish for money then spend to fish and explore better then back to fishing once more very satisfying as well, and it's paced well enough to avoid it getting stale too fast.

10/10 best game I've played all year.

Lovely Game
In Short :

- Neat progression system
- Different mechanics depending on which area you are in and what creatures you encounter
- Really nice atmosphere
- The music is a banger
- World setting is amazing
- Story isnt in the main focus here, but its not bad

- Crafting system is a bit too Grindy for my taste
- Would've loved more upgradable space for my Cargo, but the game is based around cargo space so i guess thats fair.

9/10
p.s dont go fishing late

Great game, both relaxing and atmospheric and stress inducing and terrifying at times. Nice inventory management and ship upgrade mechanic. The sailing between islands reminds me a bit of The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass.

One of favorite games of all time. It's simple yet interesting, while also balancing really well between calming and panicking. The Lovecraft theme is great, and I hope they make squeal or more DLC for the game
While i found it hard to get used to when starting out i slowly adapted to game play and before i knew it i was a dredging and fishing expert. A good game which i do recommend

Fish are scary. I didn't go in the ocean before playing this game, and I certainly won't now!

About 35 hours if you want to 100% all the achievements and the game.

Dredge is a very unusual game. If you have read H.P. Lovecraft, get ready for an adventure in that vein. The game starts off as a resource building exercise that’s fun and engrossing. Suddenly it’s 2am and you’re wondering where the hours went. What’s at the edge of the map. Why is the old guy crazy? What are the towns folks not telling me? The music is moody and fits the story very well. It’s a short game. However, it’s very well done. Great experience. Dredge will make you wonder “When I stare down into the dark sea, what’s staring back up at me?”

You know what? I'm not normally into fishing type games but Dredge had so much more to offer. Set in this sort of universe where your imagination is left to run wild of what truly is happening to your character and your surroundings while you're out sailing at night time. I fell in love with the "lovecraftian" themes intertwined into this sort of grim setting with lots of memorable characters and locations. The fish aberrations were my favorite! So much so I just had to catch them all. I highly recommend this game if anything I said speaks to you as a gamer looking for a unique and memorable experience!!
Fun lovecraftian game with a interesting story. Very cool designs for aberration fish, and the different biomes they are in. No actual combat, just sailing around fishing and solving a few puzzles.

I loved this game !

You play a fisherman in a lovecraftian world.

The gameloop is pretty simple : fish, sell fish, upgrade your gear on your boat and explore to try and explain the weird things happening since you've started this job as a fisherman.

The art style and overall ambiance of the game was so great !

While I had to grind a bit to get some of the achievements, updates since should have made it so it's not as tedious to unlock them.

I played it on the Steam Deck and while I think the controls could have been improved as far as inventory management, they were fine and I played it all the way through on the deck.

I will definetely come back when the DLC releases !

EDIT : So I did come back two years later to play both DLCs ! (Pale Breach and Iron Rig)
I enjoyed playing more of Dredge and both DLC had good stories in the same vein as the base game

I did waste quite some time catching the last types of fish as I forgot about one good trick to catch aberrations with a higher chance: use the atrophy ability. This is especially useful for the aberration of exotic fishes.

Esto da el mismo placer que chingarte una Magdalena con Nutella y leche mientras estás cobijado viendo la tele con clima lluvioso.

Muy rico y todo PERO muy caro si es arriba de $120MX. Comprar en oferta.

great game, strongly recommend it, it's a very well done lovecraftian fishing adventure.

warning: you might get spooked by scary fish, but do not worry, they just want to be friendly:)

Had much higher hopes :/ Very dull game, boring upgrades, repetetive, very abrupt ending (but in this case it was for the best). Play Dave the diver instead, much better in every aspect but simiilar gameplay loop (gather, upgrade, gather better and more, repeat).

I don't usually like fishing or fetching games, but this game hooked me from start to finish. Easy gameplay, not a lot of replayability, but I loved the atmosphere so much that I stayed until I caught them all.

The difference between the early and late game in Dredge is stark. Early on you are oppressed by the atmosphere, rarely going out after dark, scared of what's out there, below. Working up the courage to leave the starting area is the most significant and memorable hurdle in the game. The rest of it is good, it's fun the whole journey, but it never recaptures that initial feeling

Its a nice game really.
Plays best if you have the DLCs installed before you finish the main game.
Love the Game Very addicting and love the horror aspect of the game while grinding fish

I think this game is fantastic! i love the groove this game carves out of being thrilling and intriguing in its horror elements without actually ever being too scary. except when you are being chased, that's pretty horrifying. The tone in general, with the art, music, writting, and all of the creepy things hanging around really get you invested in seeing more and more of the game.

I think the actual mechanics of how you fish and how it relates to taking risks with daytime and positioning wind up being pretty engaging long term although I was a little tired of it by the very end of the game. and speaking of the end, i got both of (2 of?) the endings and im a little confused why there was such a quick and flaccid ending to the incredible and drawn out buildup of the game. there are so many elements in the game that seem to rely on their enjoyment being concluded with some incredible secret, or eldritch incredible final act, only for it be about 30 seconds of a cutscene in an unremarkable location. disappointing, but not enough to ruin the cool game that was laid before it, as the building and suspense was nice to sit in

Base game: I'm very picky about my games, but I love Dredge and recommend people try this one. The horror aspects creep in perfectly and the sound design is amazing. The art and mystery soaked story drew me in when I first saw it, and the surprises caught me off guard more times than I can count. You should make sure to play the DLC areas before finishing the base game.

Blackstone key: Gives early access to "blessed" equipment that can give you an edge in the early game, it's best to buy the bundle with all of the DLC to make this one worthwhile.

The Pale Reach: The new fish, biome, equipment, and threats are as fascinating as the overall story. This is a splendid addition to the base game.

The Iron Rig: An interesting add on to Dredge, the story of the common working man dealing with corporate bozos is always appreciated. The upgrades, side activities, equipment, and monsters are amazing.
Great experience, casual fishing meets lovecraftian horror. Solid 10-12 hours of interesting creatures, and progression with your boat as you slowly unravel what's going on.
good little indie game i would recommend it to players who have a busy schedule

I liked the game overall, but I liked the first half a LOT better than the second half (going by the recommended area order of Gale Cliffs -> Stellar Basin -> Twisted Strand -> Devil's Spine).

After seeing the big cyclops eel in Gale Cliffs I thought each area would have a cool Major Threat, some kind of sea monster to avoid. But honestly, only Gale Cliffs gets a cool sea monster. The other areas's Major Threats are quite underwhelming in comparison, being way less impressive in their presentation, mechanics or both. I'm pretty sure Twisted Strand is safer than the starting zone. I don't think it's even a matter of just having more upgrades by the time you reach those areas.

On the plus side however, I did like the fishing and went out of my way to get catch every fish and aberration in order to see all the designs. It can be a bit grindy if you want to Catch 'Em All, but to me it was worth it to see what kind of weird variant a spider crab may have, for example.

I would still recommend the game, but don't get your hopes up that later areas will have even cooler and more interesting threats to avoid.

Dredge is one massive vibe. As you commit to it, it does reveal itself to be a little too formulaic for its own good, but there are still a few interesting aspects to its mechanics and story to uncover until pretty late.

Come all ye sailors, let me tell the tale of the lone fisherman and 'bout his dark fate.

Aesome game for lovers of fishing and sailing. Put on your sailors cap and lets explore the islands.
But be aware of the dark waters and lights in the night, for deep down sleeps the danger.

I absolutely loved this game.
Yet one thing I would reproach. The music, not a single shanty and the ambient music was just someting you would soon learn to ignore.
More interesting soundtrack would make this game even more of a gem than it already is.

It's glorious, addicting, and fun. It's not necessarily the most challenging game in the world, but it's so worth it, and has enough small things to keep you busy and immersed in the game. Especially if you have a thing for side quests, and neat conversations, and creepy. And the ambiance. Play the game with sound/music, even if you normally don't - it's totally worth it. I love this game.

If you love fetch quests and reading, this is the game for you.

I'm being a little harsh, but I don't recommend it. The progression is slow, and the world layout and fishing system is not set up to allow for player freedom. It's just kinda grindy, and for my money, the mystery and horror isn't compelling or spooky enough to serve as a hook. As of the three hour mark, the gameplay loop consists of sail around, catch fish, talk to people, and upgrade your boat, none of which is challenging. If that sounds good to you, check it out, but If you want a spooky game where you truly feel out of your depth (ha ha) a la Inscryption or Darkwood, move along.
I love the story, the gameplay is fun, and the ambiance is incredible. Very relaxing at times but also love the tense and scary parts.

Very good game! It took me [Hours Played At Time of Review] to beat it. I got it on sale for $12, so it doesn't quite meet my $1/h mark of a 'good value' game, however I enjoyed all of it.

There's a pretty basic gameplay loop of just going around and fishing for either fish or consumable items that are used for upgrades. You sell fish for money, use the consumables to unlock upgrades, and then buy the upgrades with the money you got. The fishing minigames are fun and pretty varied. A good variety of different quicktime events.

The story is enjoyable, and figuring out the lore of the islands is fun! I did not play with a particularly completionist mindset, but I feel like I experienced maybe 75% of the games content in my time. Towards the end I got sort of scrap-locked, where I had oodles of money but not nearly enough supplies with which to upgrade my boat, which was a little annoying. But I reached the final tier of upgrades before this really became an issue so oh well I guess.

I would recommend this game if you think you would enjoy the atmosphere, which is superb. The gameplay is pretty fun, but the most enjoyment (for me) came from the vibes.

I should've paid full price for this. I regret getting it at a discount. 
Go into this game knowing as little as possible.
Fantasticlly atmospheric.

Unsettling game that loses its horror element the more you play, in a good way. Really gets across the feeling and mindset of being an underpaid fisherman: you don't have time to pay attention to the horrors, you just need to fish. At some point, the enemies become less scary and more annoying, and rightfully so: someone who spends all their time out on the ocean can't be worried about sharks all day.

The gameplay loop is repetitive, but enjoyable. Personally, I think that Dredge could benefit from more NPC interaction, however the atmosphere is somewhat enhanced by the lack of ties the fisherman has. Quests could also be a bit more involved, however it does make sense that they aren't. The story is easy to follow and very much unnerving, and it follows what you might expect out of a fishing horror. The one ending I've achieved is climactic, though I do wish the secret ending was more forthcoming in how you could achieve it.

If you're going for one hundred percent completion, you can get around fifteen or so hours out of Dredge. Not quite short, but it leaves you wishing there was more to experience. I'll one hundred percent recommend getting the roadmap's mentioned DLC when it comes out, and I am very much looking forward to its release. However, even without it, Dredge is very much a complete experience with a lot of technical replayability, something I would love to replay blind again.

Dredge is an amazing game. It was able to create an atmosphere of horror in a fishing game. It will remain one of my favorite games to play. Though i do not own them right now, I cant wait for what the dlc's have waiting for me.

Fantastic game. Loved the atmosphere, music and graphics. The story was poignant, and the characters were charming. Gameplay was fun, with the development of the ship and collection of different types of fish. Highly recommended!

Dredge combines satisfying fishing mechanics with an eerie, creeping horror atmosphere. The upgrade loop is excellent, and the core gameplay kept pulling me back.

Sometimes, I just wanted to fish in peace—but the eldritch elements, while not always welcome for me, do add a unique tension that sets the game apart.

I haven’t finished it yet, but I plan to. This is one of those games I know I’ll come back to when I want something haunting, methodical, and rewarding.

A simple addicting game but I do not see as one of the best of last year. 

Still not time-demanding and for the time you are in, it does worth.
Pure atmosphere. This is the perfect balance of relaxing and intense, mundane and supernatural. A master craft of juxtaposition narrative.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players praise the story and characters most, along with the gameplay.
The story and characters also draw the most complaints, while some find the grind repetitive.

details.text: 3% of recent reviews complain about the price, down sharply from the all-time level.
Early players are less positive, at 81%, while long-time players reach 99%.
